To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the four HHT1 point mutations analyzed lead to reduced levels of fully processed normal protein and to intracellular mutant species which do not interfere with endoglin function.
four missense mutations in the ENDOGLIN gene lead to haploinsuffiency, i.e. reduced levels of endoglin, and thus cause hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia type I (HHT1), a vascular disorder.
the four missense mutations lead, in all cases, to reduced expression of fully glycosylated, mature endoglin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the vascular dysplasia hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia (HHT).
the expression and function of endoglin and the molecular mechanisms underlying the HHT phenotype.

the study of the molecular basis of hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia (HHT), an autosomal dominant vascular disease characterized by the formation of telangiectases, arteriovenous malformations (AVM) and aneurysms, which may lead to serious hemorrhage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all known HHT1 mutations lead to haploinsufficieny.
all missense mutations in endoglin result in a reduction in the amount of endoglin at the surface of endothelial cells, leading to haploinsufficency.
all missense mutations lead, in the same way, to the synthesis of a truncated endoglin protein, which is not able to reach the cell surface and is not functional.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HHT1 mutations are not all equivalent.
HHT1 patients have reduced levels of endoglin, which is not functional, and that the HHT1 clinical phenotype can be attributed to the haploinsufficent expression of endoglin.
the endoglin mutations found in HHT1 patients are not expressed on the surface of endothelial cells and monocytes, and that the mutant proteins remain intracellular.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HHT1 mutations lead to haploinsufficency, not dominant negative activity.
haploinsufficient mutations in ENDOGLIN are responsible for HHT1, and that these mutations result in a reduction in the levels of ENDOGLIN at the plasma membrane of vascular endothelial cells.
haploinsufficient expression of endoglin is a common feature of HHT1.
